full_judgment:
This Rule under section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of defendant No. 1 Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation is directed against the judgment and decree of the learned Sub-ordinate judge 3rd Court, Chittagong, passed in other appeal No. 150 of 1982, dismissing the appeal and allowing the cross-objection and affirming the judgment and decree of the learned Munsif, 1st Court at Sadar, Chittagong passed in other suit No. 147 of 1981. 

 2. The opposite-parties Nos. 1-16 as plaintiffs filed the suit against the defendant No. 1 petitioner and defendant No. 2, Bangladesh for declaration, inter alia, (a) that the plaintiffs and other loanees of the defendant No. 1 for the Multi-storied Housing Scheme with floor space limit of 1500 sft. Per unit are not liable to pay interest and monthly repayment of installments at any rate higher than the rate specified in their respective sanction letters; (b) that the defendants have got no right or authority to unilaterally change the terms and conditions of the loan agreement contained in the sanction letters and/or change the rate of interest and monthly repayment installments and have no right to demand payment of interest at any rate higher than the amount specified in the sanction letters: (c) that the Circular No. MF. Inv-IV/HBFC/23/77/15 dated 20-1-1981 of the Ministry of Finance (Banking & Investment Division), Investment Wing section-IV of defendant No. 2 and the letter of defendant No. 1 dated 26-2-81 demanding rate of interest at 7½% per annum, are wholly illegal, against the provision of contract, malafide, unauthorized, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs and other loanees and (d) that a decree of permanent injunction be passed restraining the defendants from demanding or realizing interest and/or monthly repayments from the plaintiffs and other loanees who were granted loans on the Multi-storied Housing Scheme with floor space of 1500 sft. Per unit at any rate higher than the 5% interest and repayment instalments at any amount higher the amount fixed in the sanction letters. 

 9. The learned Munsif decreed the suit in part declaring that the plaintiffs are not liable to pay rate of interest and instalment other then specified in their respective sanction letters and restraining the defendants permanently from demanding and realizing any rate of interest other than 5% and amount of instalment of loans other than fixed by the sanction letters, holding the view that the sanction letter and the mortgage deed together form the contract but since according to the plaintiffs documents like in interest does not relate to 1500 sft. Floor space per unit, the circular dated 26-2-81 does not apply in the case of the plaintiffs and so the letters Exhibits 3-3(E) are illegal and out of jurisdiction. 

 10. Against the judgment and decree of the learned Munsif the defendant No. 1 corporation filed the appeal and against the observation of the learned Munsif that sanction letter and mortgage deeds together form the contract the plaintiff filed cross-objection. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge who heard both the appeal and cross-objection. Dismissed the appeal but allowed the cross-objection and decreed the suit in full holding the view the sanction letter along with mortgage deed cannot form the contract of loan and the observation of the learned Munsif that the sanction letter and mortgage deed form the contract, is not correct. 

 For the reason stated above and having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record, I am of the view that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has rightly decreed the suit and his decision does not suffer from any error, illegality or flaw causing failure of justice for interference. In the result, the Rule is discharged but without any order as to costs.
